rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing clause is a coda: if the able are intended, it recalls fasting’s worldly benefits and afterlife reward; otherwise it recalls the reward under the alternative readings. إن marks uncertain knowledge because both benefits are hidden.
rows.anchor: تذييل أي تعلمون فوائد الصوم على رجوعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses continue the preceding fasting verses, and there is no abrogation among them.
rows.anchor: قد علمت أن هذه الآيات تكملة للآيات السابقة وأن لا نسخ في خلال هاته الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase predicates Ramadan of an omitted subject, meaning the specified counted days are Ramadan; it resumes the discussion to answer the question raised by “counted days.”
rows.anchor: خبر مبتدأ محذوف تقديره هي أي الأيام المعدودات شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reads شهرا in the accusative as a detailed apposition to أيامًا, supporting the omitted-subject analysis.
rows.anchor: ويؤيد ذلك قراءة مجاهد { شهرا } بالنصب على البدلية من { أياما } : بدل تفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If this verse abrogated the preceding rule, Ramadan could instead be the subject, with the following clause as its predicate; the conditional-like relative licenses its فاء, or the فاء is extra as in Sibawayh’s poetic example. Both analyses are weak.
rows.anchor: أنشده سيبويه ، وكلا هذين الوجهين ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A month is one of twelve divisions of the year, running from one new crescent to the next; it is named from شهرة because the visible crescent is publicized. The verse on twelve months is linked.
rows.anchor: والشهر جزء من اثني عشر جزءا من تقسيم السنة قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ramadan is the recurring lunar month assigned for the obligatory fast; because the time recurs each year, the obligation recurs annually and is not limited to one particular Ramadan.
rows.anchor: فكلما حل الوقت المعين من السنة المسمى بشهر رمضان فقد وجب على المسلمين أداء فريضة الصوم فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause may recall a great virtue the audience already knows, since the Quran’s descent is a major religious event unlikely to be obscure.
rows.anchor: أن المخاطبين يعلمون أن نزول القرآن وقع في شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the clause can inform the audience of Ramadan’s virtue and identify it through this unique attribute; familiarity with a relative clause’s content is usual, not required.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أيضا أن يكون إعلاما بهذا الفضل وأجري الكلام على طريقة الوصف بالموصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence is not simply reporting that Ramadan is the month of Quranic revelation: شهر رمضان is a predicate, not the subject, in this construction.
rows.anchor: وليس المقصود الإخبار عن شهر رمضان بأنه أنزل فيه القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran’s descent means its beginning was revealed to the Prophet in year forty-one of the Elephant era; the first portion stands for the whole whose completion was destined to follow, as in 6:92.
rows.anchor: فإن فيه ابتداء النزول من عام واحد وأربعين من الفيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In it” means in a corresponding Ramadan of another year: the actual month of first revelation had passed years before fasting became obligatory in the second year after the Hijra.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { الذي أنزل فيه } أنزل في مثله

words: هدى للناس وبينات من الهدى والفرقان
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two descriptions are circumstantial clauses referring to the Quran; they show why the month is favored because guidance and distinction were revealed in it.
rows.anchor: حالان من ( القرآن ) إشارة بهما إلى وجه تفضيل الشهر بسبب ما نزل فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first guidance is the Quran’s direction toward public and private interests that do not conflict with the common good.
rows.anchor: ما في القرآن من الإرشاد إلى المصالح العامة والخاصة التي لا تنافي العامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear proofs establish less visible guidance that many reject, including arguments for divine oneness, the Messenger’s truth, and other Quranic proofs.
rows.anchor: ما في القرآن من الاستدلال على الهدى الخفي الذي ينكره كثير من الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Furqan means the Quran’s public distinction between truth from God and the falsehood people followed before Islam; the two kinds of guidance are therefore not repetitive.
rows.anchor: والفرقان مصدر فرق وقد شاع في الفرق بين الحق والباطل أي إعلان التفرقة بين الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse returns to explaining the fasting command after an interlude that reassured listeners, praised fasting’s benefit for piety, and noted the easing of hardship.
rows.anchor: فهو رجوع إلى التبيين بعد الفصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Among you” refers back to the believers addressed in the fasting command.
rows.anchor: عائد إلى { الذين أمنوا } ( البقرة : 183 ) مثل الضمائر التي قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If شهد means attended, الشهر is an adverbial object: whoever is present during the month, rather than traveling, must fast it; anyone present for only part fasts those days.
rows.anchor: { شهد } يجوز أن يكون بمعنى حضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: شهد may instead mean knew the month had arrived, with an understood word for its arrival; it does not mean saw, nor does الشهر here mean the crescent as al-Zajjaj reports from usage.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { شهد } بمعنى علم كقوله تعالى

words: ومن كان مريضا أو على سفر فعدة من أيام أخر
rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: On the view that 2:185 abrogates the earlier choice of fasting or feeding, the repeated exemption preserves make-up fasting for the sick and traveler while abrogating feeding for healthy residents.
rows.anchor: أنه لما كان صوم رمضان واجبا على التخيير بينه وبين الفدية بالإطعام بالآية الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If both passages were revealed together, the exemption is repeated where it best fits, after the fasting days are specified; the earlier mention gave listeners advance reassurance.
rows.anchor: كان الوجه في إعادة هذا الحكم هو هذا الموضع الجدير

words: ومن كان مريضا أو على سفر فعدة من أيام أخر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repetition can also prevent readers from thinking the first exemption was abrogated by شهد, if understood as knowing the month; it reinforces and clarifies the concession.
rows.anchor: شهد بمعنى تحقق وعلم ، مع زيادة في تأكيد حكم الرخصة

words: ومن كان مريضا أو على سفر فعدة من أيام أخر
يريد الله بكم اليسر ولا يريد بكم العسر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This explanatory resumption gives the reason for the exemption: God legislates making up missed fasts to provide ease when hardship occurs.
rows.anchor: بين به حكمة الرخصة أي شرع لكم القضاء

words: يريد الله بكم اليسر ولا يريد بكم العسر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A single restriction to ease could have expressed the meaning, but affirmation comes first as the reason for the concession, then negation emphasizes it.
rows.anchor: لكنه عدل عن جملة القصر إلى جملتي إثبات ونفي لأن المقصود ابتداء هو جملة الإثبات

words: يريد الله بكم اليسر ولا يريد بكم العسر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may explain all the preceding legislation: fasting may look difficult, yet its benefits make it an easy form of self-discipline, unlike other religions’ self-imposed strain.
rows.anchor: إيماء إلى أن مشروعية الصيام وإن كانت تلوح في صورة المشقة والعسر

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: The majority read اليسر and العسر with a still س; Abu Jaafar reads both with a damma by vowel harmony.
rows.anchor: بسكون السين فيهما ، وقرأه أبو جعفر بضم السين ضمة إتباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in ولتكبروا is شبه زائدة: after wanting or commanding, a مصدر clause normally takes no preposition, though the lām is common; its verb is subjunctive after explicit or understood أن. Al-Kashshaf cites 61:8 and 39:12.
rows.anchor: تسمى شبه الزائدة وهي اللام التي يكثر وقوعها بعد فعل الإرادة وفعل الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction continues the explanation: all four clauses from witnessing the month through making up missed days explain the preceding command.
rows.anchor: فإن مجموع هذه الجمل الأربع تعليل لما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Completing the count means making up days missed by those required to fast, preserving the wisdom of a complete Ramadan; the concession for an excuse supplies mercy and relief.
rows.anchor: وإكمال العدة يحصل بقضاء الأيام التي أفطرها من وجب عليه الصوم ليأتي بعدة أيام شهر رمضان كاملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read ولتكملوا with a still ك and light م from أكمل; Abu Bakr from Asim and Yaqub read it with a fatḥa and doubled م from كمل.
rows.anchor: مضارع أكمل وقرأه أبو بكر عن عاصم ويعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takbir verbally attributes greatness to God: say الله أكبر, declaring divine majesty and transcendence from every deficiency; the verb is coined from the phrase, like basmala and hamdala.
rows.anchor: والتكبير تفعيل مراد به النسبة والتوصيف أي أن تنسبوا الله إلى الكبر والنسبة هنا نسبة بالقول اللساني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is greater than every actual or imagined power; affirming this entails His unique divinity, since whatever else is deficient cannot deserve worship.
rows.anchor: لأن التفضيل يستلزم نقصان من عداه والناقص غير مستحق للإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takbir was prescribed in prayer to end prostration to other than God and when sacrificing in pilgrimage to end offerings to idols; this verse also grounds takbir at the end of fasting.
rows.anchor: عند نحر البدن في الحج لإبطال ما كانوا يتقربون به إلى أصنامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse grounds the established practice of Muslims saying takbir while setting out for Eid prayer and the imam saying it in the Eid sermon.
rows.anchor: فمن أجل ذلك مضت السنة بأن يكبر المسلمون عند الخروج إلى صلاة العيد ويكبر الإمام في خطبة العيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eid takbir counters the idolaters’ attempts to approach their gods through food and blood: Muslims’ takbir signals that God is worshipped through fasting and is above idol worship.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أن الله يعبد بالصوم وأنه متنزه عن ضراوة الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gratitude is a broader rationale than takbir: it includes spoken glorification, charitable acts during fasting and Eid, and wearing fine clothes on Eid.
rows.anchor: لأنه يكون بالأقوال التي فيها تعظيم لله تعالى ويكون بفعل القرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse commands takbir but leaves its wording, timing, and number unspecified; Prophetic practice clarifies these, with juristic differences.
rows.anchor: وهو غير مفصل في لفظ التكبير

rows.speaker: مالك وأبو حنيفة والشافعي
rows.claim: The famous Sunnah formula repeats الله أكبر three times, and Malik, Abu Hanifa, and al-Shafii adopt it.
rows.anchor: والمشهور في السنة أنه يكرر الله أكبر ثلاثا

rows.speaker: مالك والشافعي
rows.claim: Malik and al-Shafii permit added tahlil and praise after two takbirs; Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas are cited for saying لا إله إلا الله والله أكبر ولله الحمد.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك والشافعي : إذا شاء المرء زاد على التكبير

rows.speaker: أحمد
rows.claim: Ahmad holds that the formula is flexible.
rows.anchor: وقال أحمد : هو واسع

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa holds that fewer or other than three takbirs do not suffice.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة : لا يجزىء غير ثلاث تكبيرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eid takbir begins when worshippers and imam leave home for the prayer place and stops when they arrive.
rows.anchor: فتكبير الفطر يبتدىء من وقت خروج المصلي من بيته إلى محل الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The strongest practice is seven extra takbirs in the first Eid rakah and six in the second, supported by reports and Medinan practice from the Prophet onward; many disputes exist, but the matter is broad.
rows.anchor: هذا هو الأصح مما ثبت في الأخبار وعمل به أهل المدينة من عهد النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After prayer, the imam says takbir in the Eid sermon; congregants repeat during his takbir and listen to the sermon otherwise.
rows.anchor: ثم يكبر الإمام في خطبة صلاة العيد بعد الصلاة ويكبر معه المصلون حين تكبيره وينصتون للخطبة

words: ليس عليكم جناح أن تبتغوا فضلا من ربكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permission to seek trade is an interpolated statement between linked clauses: it rejects the pagan scruple that commerce during pilgrimage conflicts with Hajj’s purpose.
rows.anchor: جملة معترضة بين المتعاطفين بمناسبة النهي عن أعمال في الحج تنافي المقصد منه فنقل الكلام إلى إباحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here فضل means wealth, and seeking it means trading for profit; the phrasing parallels 73:20.
rows.anchor: التجارة لأجل الربح كما هو

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Ukaz, Majanna, and Dhul-Majaz were pre-Islamic markets where pilgrims feared trading during the seasons; the verse was revealed permitting it, and he read an added phrase, “during Hajj season.”
rows.anchor: في الجاهلية فتأثموا أن يتجروا في المواسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before Islam, Ukaz opened at the start of Dhu al-Qadah for twenty days, followed by Majanna and Dhul-Majaz; Ukaz featured fine goods, tribal boasts, and poetry contests near Nakhla and Taif.
rows.anchor: وقد كانت سوق عكاظ تفتح مستهل ذي القعدة وتدوم عشرين يوما وفيها تباع نفائس السلع وتتفاخر القبائل

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nabigha’s poem witnesses that trade had stopped at Dhul-Majaz during the pilgrimage season.
rows.anchor: كادت تساقطني رحلي وميثرتي بذي المجاز ولم تحسس به نغما

words: فإذا أفضتم من عرفات فاذكروا الله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The فاء links the command to the preceding prohibition in 2:197; إذا أفضتم is the condition for the intended command, فاذكروا الله.
rows.anchor: شرط للمقصود وهو : ( فاذكروا الله )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: المشعر may derive from awareness or from a sign; a marker may have helped the many pilgrims leaving Arafat at dusk avoid losing their way.
rows.anchor: اسم مشتق من الشعور أي العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called sacred because the site lies within the Haram, unlike Arafat.
rows.anchor: لأنه من أرض الحرم بخلاف عرفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sacred station is Muzdalifa, also called Muzdalifa because it is near Mina, where pilgrims intend to be by morning; it is called Jam because all pilgrims assembled there even before Islam, not because they combined prayers.
rows.anchor: سميت مزدلفة لأنها ازدلفت من منى أي اقتربت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation that Jam means the place where Maghrib and Isha are combined is mistaken, since the name predates Islam.
rows.anchor: إن تسميتها جمعا لأنها يجمع فيها بين المغرب والعشاء فقد غفل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muzdalifa is also Qazah, a mountain spur at its edge; it is called al-Miqaada because pre-Islamic Arabs lit fires there, and it was Quraysh’s station and the imam’s stopping point.
rows.anchor: لأن العرب في الجاهلية كانوا يوقدون عليه النيران

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi report that the Prophet went to Qazah at dawn at Jam, stood there, and said that Qazah is the station while all of Jam is a station; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: لما أصبح بجمع أتى قزح فوقف عليه

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik holds that spending the night at Muzdalifa is Sunnah, while remaining there for some time is obligatory.
rows.anchor: ومذهب مالك أن المبيت سنة وأما النزول حصة فواجب

rows.speaker: علقمة والأوزاعي وجماعة من التابعين
rows.claim: Alqama, al-Awzai, and a group of Successors regard standing at Muzdalifa as a pillar of Hajj; missing it invalidates the pilgrimage, based on the command to remember God there.
rows.anchor: وذهب علقمة وجماعة من التابعين والأوزاعي إلى أن الوقوف بمزدلفة ركن من الحج فمن فاته بطل حجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before Islam, Banu Sufa, descendants of Ghawth ibn Murra, controlled departure from Arafat; Ghawth’s mother had vowed a son to serve the Kaaba, and wool tied to a vowed child’s hair was called al-rabit. Qusayy later granted his descendants the permit.
rows.anchor: وقد كانت العرب في الجاهلية لا يفيضون من عرفة إلى المزدلفة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative account says the kings of Kinda, rather than Qusayy, assigned Ghawth’s descendants the authority to release pilgrims.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن الذي جعل أبناء الغوث لإجازة الحاج هم ملوك كندة

words: ثم أفيضوا من حيث أفاض الناس
rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation takes the command as departure from Muzdalifa to Mina, after remembrance at the sacred station; the author says this sequence followed an old Abrahamic practice, later administered by Khuzaa then Banu Adwan.
rows.anchor: الإفاضة من مزدلفة إلى منى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the old practice, pilgrims left Muzdalifa on the tenth after sunrise on Thabir; Abu Sayyara led on a black donkey after a prayer and the call “Shine, Thabir, so we may go.”
rows.anchor: وكانوا في الجاهلية يخرجون من مزدلفة يوم عاشر ذي الحجة بعد أن تطلع الشمس على ثبير

rows.speaker: أبو سيارة
rows.claim: The authorization passed from Khuzaa to Banu Adwan; Abu Sayyara, Amila ibn al-Az’al, held it for forty years until Mecca’s conquest, when the rite ended and pilgrims followed the Hajj leader.
rows.anchor: وكان آخر من تولى الإجازة منهم أبا سيارة عميلة بن الأعزل أجاز بالناس أربعين سنة إلى أن فتحت مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase refers to Muzdalifa, the place from which the people depart, because all Arabs assembled there.
rows.anchor: أي من المكان الذي يفيض منه سائر الناس وهو مزدلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without the relevant hadith, departure from Muzdalifa to Mina would be textually clearer: it would state both departures explicitly and lead naturally into completing the rites in 2:200.
rows.anchor: ولولا ما جاء من الحديث لكان هذا التفسير أظهر لتكون الآية ذكرت الإفاضتين بالصراحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command follows the departure from Muzdalifa to Mina, explicitly or by implication; Mina is where stoning occurs, and the verse points to stoning Aqaba on the tenth, then sacrifice and completion of Hajj.
rows.anchor: لأن تلك الإفاضة هي الدفع من مزدلفة إلى منى أو لأنها تستلزم ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars agree that on the Day of Sacrifice the pilgrim stones only Aqaba, from sunrise until noon, then sacrifices, performs the circumambulation of ifada, and completes Hajj; all becomes permitted except sex.
rows.anchor: وقد أجمعوا على أن الحاج لا يرمي يوم النحر إلا جمرة العقبة من بعد طلوع الشمس إلى الزوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مناسك is the plural of mansak, from worship; here it is best taken as a verbal noun after قضيتم, though it could mean a place and require an omitted noun. The same term occurs in 2:128.
rows.anchor: منسك مشتق من نسك نسكا من باب نصر إذا تعبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All readers pronounce the two ك sounds separately; al-Susi from Abu Amr merges them by the major assimilation.
rows.anchor: بفك الكافين وقرأه السوسي عن أبي عمرو بإدغامهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The renewed command encourages remembrance after remembrance and asking forgiveness, countering pre-Islamic idle talk and boasting that led to argument; pilgrims should be immersed in worship in deed, speech, and belief.
rows.anchor: أعاد الأمر بالذكر بعد أن أمر به وبالاستغفار تحضيضا عليه وإبطالا لما كانوا عليه في الجاهلية من الاشتغال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison describes the manner of remembrance; the prepositional phrase modifies an omitted verbal noun, “remembrance.”
rows.anchor: فالجار والمجرور نعت لمصدر محذوف أي ذكرا كذكركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison recalls pilgrims filling their time at Mina by boasting about ancestry and past tribal exploits between the mosque site and the mountain beginning at the Aqaba stoning place.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ما كانوا عليه من الاشتغال في أيام منى بالتفاخر بالأنساب ومفاخر أيامهم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi reports that a man would boast that his father had a great tent, a large bowl, and much wealth, then ask God for the same; he would mention nothing else, and similar statements were reported.
rows.anchor: كان الرجل يقوم فيقول : اللهم إن أبي كان عظيم القبة عظيم الجفنة كثير المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison calls for frequent, repeated remembrance that fills free time; it does not suggest combining remembrance of God with remembrance of fathers.
rows.anchor: والمراد تشبيه ذكر الله بذكر آبائهم في الكثرة والتكرير وتعمير أوقات الفراغ به وليس فيه ما يؤذن بالجمع
